# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b93 — accurate native device names and dual entity links

Beta93 builds directly on the published Beta92 Lovelace scroll-jump fix.

## Controller versus physical device

- **Folded device title:** retains the Home Environment Manager controller's own name and opens **the HEM controller entity** in Home Assistant More Info. Clicking the title does not expand/collapse the device fold.
- **Folded device icon:** continues to open the authorized native physical entity when a verified source exists.
- **Expanded device title:** displays the **native Home Assistant physical device's actual `friendly_name`**, not HEM's autogenerated facade name, controller suffix, or a concatenation of the two. Clicking this title opens the original physical device entity, not the HEM controller.
- The physical native source is selected only from HEM's declared `physical_primary_entity_id` and its exact registered `source_entity_ids`, or from a single unambiguous source. Conflicting or ambiguous source metadata disables the physical title link rather than guessing an unrelated entity.
- Native integration renames update the expanded heading on the next HA state update. Controllers keep their name even if the physical device is renamed.
- Preserve focus, folded/expanded state, mobile layout, native More Info navigation, and Beta92 page-level scroll recovery.

## Tests and safety

A real Chromium regression tests the exact paired link behavior, native HA friendly name, live native rename, multiple physical sources, a forged/stale physical link, and narrow-screen layout. Existing Beta87–92 DOM, controller/card interactions, real native safety, dehumidifier DRY-only PWM, restart continuity, physical acknowledgement, window protection and compressor minimum ON/OFF tests remain release gates.

**Frontend and manifest only:** No device-control, PID, HA service permissions, native state ownership or power-switch Python source has been changed.

## Install

Use HACS prereleases to update Home Environment Manager to **v0.6.0b93**, then restart Home Assistant if required and hard-refresh the Lovelace page (`Ctrl+Shift+R`) to invalidate previously cached frontend JavaScript.
